hero.description: This map shows points of interest in the days before the Battle of Droop Mountain that occurred in West Virginia during November 1863. gallery.title: File:William W. Averell.jpg
gallery.credit: Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries  The exact same photo was published near the front of History of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry, Sixtieth Regiment Pennsylvania Volunteers, in the American Civil War, 1861-1865., Volume 3, Part 4, which was published by the Franklin Printing Company in Philadelphia in 1905. The author is listed as United States, 3rd Pennsylvania Calvary Regiment. The cover of the book says William Brooke Rawie, and the inside says "Compiled by the Regimental History Committee in Accordance with a Resolution of the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry Association." The OCLC number is 1683643.
gallery.description: William Woods Averell (1832–1900) was a United States Army officer and a cavalry general in the American Civil War. After the war he was a diplomat and became wealthy by inventing American asphalt pavement.

gallery.artist: G.W. & C.B. Colton published map in 1876, modifications by TwoScarsUp in 2020
gallery.credit: This is two portions of an 1876 map created by G.W. & C.B. Colton & Co.  The entire map can be found in the Library of Congress here, and shows Virginia and West Virginia. Text box and arrows etc. were added by TwoScarsUp based on description in the book Last Sleep - the Battle of Droop Mountain by Terry Lowry.
gallery.source: Skirmish at Mill Point WV Step 2
gallery.description: The map shows Union and Confederate troop movements leading to a skirmish at Mill Point, West Virginia, on November 5, 1863. Additional troops for both sides fought on the next day 11 miles (18 km) south in the Battle of Droop Mountain. Schoonmaker took the southern route for the Union.  Oley took the west-then-south route. Arnett took the CSA route (red).

gallery.title: File:Battle of Droop Mountain map.png
gallery.artist: United States War Department (much of the work was done by Robert N. Scott, Joseph W. Kirkley, and Fred C. Ainsworth.
gallery.description: This is a United States War Department map of the Droop Mountain battlefield, including positions of the Union and Confederate armies. The Battle occurred on November 6, 1863, with the Union force led by William W. Averell defeating a Confederate Force led by John Echols. The map's orientation is somewhat "upside down", as Hillsborough is actually northeast of Droop Mountain.

gallery.title: File:Droop Mtn Troop Movements.png
gallery.description: This is a map that shows the Union troop movements of November 1863 in West Virginia. The plan was to capture Lewisburg and then move south to disable the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad, but the Battle of Droop Mountain happened instead.

gallery.artist: United States War Department (much of the work was done by Robert N. Scott, Joseph W. Kirkley, and Fred C. Ainsworth. The map was drawn from a partial survey by Henry Topping.
gallery.description: This is a United States War Department map of the Droop Mountain battlefield, including positions of the Union and Confederate armies. The Battle occurred on November 6, 1863, with the Union force led by William W. Averell defeating a Confederate Force led by John Echols. The map's orientation is somewhat "upside down", as the top of the map is south. The point of view is Averell's (approaching from the north) as the right side of the map is Averell's right and Echols' left.
